MS: Minus; used to indicate a negative value or below-zero condition
MSA: Minimum sector altitude; the lowest altitude that provides obstacle clearance within a sector
MSAW: Minimum safe altitude warning; a system-generated alert when an aircraft is below a predetermined safe altitude
MSG: Message; used in NOTAM text to denote a message or communication item
MSL: Mean sea level; the standard vertical datum for altitude and elevation measurement
MT: Mountain; used in NOTAMs to indicate terrain-related hazards or references
MTOM: Maximum take-off mass; the maximum permissible mass of an aircraft at take-off
MTU: Metric units; indicates that values are expressed in the metric system
MTW: Mountain waves; atmospheric gravity waves caused by airflow over mountains, a known aviation hazard
MWO: Meteorological watch office; an office that monitors weather conditions and issues significant meteorological information (SIGMET)
NASC: National AIS system center; the national authority responsible for Aeronautical Information Services (AIS)
NAV: Navigation; used in NOTAMs to refer to navigation equipment, procedures, or status
NAVAID: Navigation aid; a ground-based or space-based facility that provides position guidance to aircraft
NB: Northbound; indicates direction of flight or movement toward the north
NBFR: Not before ...; indicates that a specified condition or event will not occur earlier than the given time
NC: No change; indicates that no alteration has occurred to a reported condition
NDB: Non-directional radio beacon; a ground-based radio transmitter used for aircraft navigation
NE: North-east; the direction midway between north and east
NEB: North-eastbound; indicates direction of flight or movement toward the north-east
NGT: Night; used to indicate conditions or restrictions applicable during nighttime hours
NM: Nautical miles; a unit of distance used in aviation and maritime navigation, equal to 1,852 metres
NML: Normal; indicates that a system or condition is operating as expected
NN: No name, unnamed; used when a feature, waypoint, or object has no designated name
NNE: North-north-east; the direction between north and north-east
NNW: North-north-west; the direction between north and north-west
NOF: International NOTAM office; the office responsible for the international exchange of NOTAMs
NONSTD: Non-standard; indicates that a procedure, equipment, or condition deviates from the standard specification
NOTAMC: Cancelling NOTAM; a NOTAM series that cancels a previously issued NOTAM
NOTAMN: New NOTAM; a NOTAM series for newly issued NOTAM information
NOTAMR: Replacing NOTAM; a NOTAM series that replaces a previously issued NOTAM with updated information
NOV: November; the eleventh month of the year (November 11 used in date/time groups)
NPA: Non-precision approach; an instrument approach that provides lateral guidance but no vertical guidance
NR: Number; used to denote a numerical identifier, such as a NOTAM sequence number
NRH: No reply heard; indicates that no response was received from a radio call
NS: Nimbostratus; a low-level, dark cloud layer producing continuous precipitation
NSC: Nil significant cloud; indicates no cloud of operational significance is present
NSE: Navigation system error; the difference between the actual and indicated position from a navigation system
NSW: Nil significant weather; indicates no weather phenomena of operational significance are present
NTL: National; used to indicate that a condition, restriction, or service applies at the national level
NTZ: No transgression zone; a defined airspace area that aircraft must not enter
NW: North-west; the direction midway between north and west
NWB: North-westbound; indicates direction of flight or movement toward the north-west
NXT: Next; used to indicate the subsequent occurrence or sequential item
O/R: On request; indicates that a service or clearance is available only upon pilot request
OAC: Oceanic area control centre; an air traffic control unit managing airspace over ocean areas
OAS: Obstacle assessment surface; an inclined plane used to evaluate obstacle clearance for instrument procedures
OBST: Obstacle; any fixed or mobile object that may pose a hazard to aircraft operations
OCA: Obstacle clearance altitude; the lowest altitude above sea level that provides required obstacle clearance
OCC: Occulting (light); a type of light signal where the periods of light are longer than the periods of darkness
OCH: Obstacle clearance height; the lowest height above the runway threshold providing required obstacle clearance
